mira.work_line: Sorting seedlings for the hillside clinic is quieter than it looks.
mira.rain_line: Rain brings the scent of crushed mint into my workshop.

seasonal_lines.Spring: The hillside herbs are waking. I leave the first blossoms for the bees.
seasonal_lines.Summer: I dry each leaf in the shade so its scent survives the heat.
seasonal_lines.Autumn: The last roots need careful hands before the ground cools.
seasonal_lines.Winter: My windowsill garden keeps a little green alive through the frost.

mira.bond_line: I remember the small kindnesses you never announce.
mira.festival_line: The lantern path feels warmer when neighbors walk it together.
mira.gift_memory_favorite: I tucked the %s into my herb journal. Its color still makes me smile.
mira.gift_memory_preferred: I used the %s you brought while sorting my field notes. That was thoughtful.

rowan.work_line: Measure twice, listen three times, and the old bridge might stand another winter.
rowan.rain_line: Rain is useful: it shows which roof still needs my attention.

seasonal_lines.Spring: A new fence is a promise to the seedlings behind it.
seasonal_lines.Summer: The sun has made every board warm to the touch.
seasonal_lines.Autumn: I save the best timber for repairs before the first freeze.
seasonal_lines.Winter: Even a quiet workshop has stories in its wood shavings.

rowan.bond_line: You helped this place feel worth building for.
rowan.festival_line: I made the festival benches from reclaimed orchard wood.
rowan.gift_memory_favorite: That %s you brought had a lovely grain. I saved it for a careful repair.
rowan.gift_memory_preferred: The %s you shared helped me finish a small piece of work. Thank you.

celia.work_line: The oven is ready; every loaf has to earn its place at the table.
celia.rain_line: The rain taps the bakery awning like impatient little customers.

seasonal_lines.Spring: Rhubarb and berries will make the market smell like morning.
seasonal_lines.Summer: I keep a pitcher of cold berry tea for anyone working outside.
seasonal_lines.Autumn: There is no better sound than crust cracking beside a warm hearth.
seasonal_lines.Winter: The kitchen windows fog up with stories and cinnamon.

celia.bond_line: I saved the corner piece for you. I know you like the crisp edge.
celia.festival_line: We set an extra place at the long table for newcomers.
celia.gift_memory_favorite: I kept the %s you brought for a special kitchen experiment. It made the morning brighter.
celia.gift_memory_preferred: Your %s gave me a new idea for the village table.

orion.work_line: I mend the nets, but I never take more from the lake than it can spare.
orion.rain_line: A rainy lake is a thousand tiny mirrors.

seasonal_lines.Spring: The first silver fish return when the reeds turn bright.
seasonal_lines.Summer: At dusk the lake holds the whole sky without spilling it.
seasonal_lines.Autumn: The water grows still enough to hear a single falling leaf.
seasonal_lines.Winter: I check the ice before anyone sets foot near the shore.

orion.bond_line: You understand that patience is a kind of courage.
orion.festival_line: The lake lanterns are made from paper, not promises.
orion.gift_memory_favorite: I remember that %s. It reminded me why the lake deserves patient hands.
orion.gift_memory_preferred: The %s you shared made a long afternoon by the pier feel shorter.

alba.work_line: The youngest animals always eat first. They trust us to remember.
alba.rain_line: I make sure every creature has a dry corner before a storm.

seasonal_lines.Spring: The barn wakes earlier when new chicks start peeping.
seasonal_lines.Summer: The animals seek the cool shade by the orchard wall.
seasonal_lines.Autumn: I lay extra straw before the nights grow sharp.
seasonal_lines.Winter: Warm water and a gentle voice do wonders on a frozen morning.

alba.bond_line: You notice when a small creature needs help. That matters.
alba.festival_line: The festival garlands are woven with fallen leaves, never fresh nests.
alba.gift_memory_favorite: The %s you brought helped me make the barn feel welcoming.
alba.gift_memory_preferred: I remember your %s. The little acts of care matter here.

soren.work_line: I am cataloguing letters, not secrets. The difference is consent.
soren.rain_line: Rain makes the old pages curl; I keep the windows latched.

seasonal_lines.Spring: The oldest map shows a path hidden by the new meadow.
seasonal_lines.Summer: The library is cool enough for long afternoons of questions.
seasonal_lines.Autumn: Every fallen leaf is a note in the valley's yearly ledger.
seasonal_lines.Winter: The village history has blank pages. We get to write the next ones.

soren.bond_line: I trust you with stories that are not mine to give away lightly.
soren.festival_line: I will read the names of the people who planted this square.
soren.gift_memory_favorite: I wrote a note about the %s you brought, so its story would not be lost.
soren.gift_memory_preferred: Your %s has found a place in my memory, even if not on the archive shelves.

festivals.name: Seed Lantern Walk
festivals.narration: Paper lanterns light the path where neighbors once shared seeds.

festivals.name: Lake of Stars
festivals.narration: Families fold blue lanterns for the lake, then return them safely to shore.

festivals.name: The Hearth Table
festivals.narration: Everyone brings a story to the table; nobody is asked to arrive with food.

festivals.name: Frostglass Bells
festivals.narration: The village rings handmade glass bells to welcome the returning light.

text.en: After we sorted those herbs together, I found a quiet place for the seedlings you saved.
text.es: Después de ordenar aquellas hierbas, encontré un rincón tranquilo para las plántulas que salvaste.

text.en: Thank you for helping in the garden. The young mint has room to breathe now.
text.es: Gracias por ayudar en el jardín. La menta joven ya tiene espacio para crecer.

text.en: You've become someone I trust with the bridge's oldest beams. We'll repair them without rushing.
text.es: Ya confío en ti para cuidar las vigas más antiguas del puente. Las repararemos sin prisas.

text.en: The boards you sanded fit the market bench. Come see how steady it feels.
text.es: Las tablas que lijaste encajan en el banco del mercado. Ven a ver qué firme quedó.

text.en: You've earned a place beside the oven when we plan the village's shared table.
text.es: Te has ganado un lugar junto al horno cuando preparamos la mesa común del pueblo.

text.en: That dough you kneaded rose beautifully. Even the early customers noticed.
text.es: La masa que amasaste subió de maravilla. Hasta los primeros clientes lo notaron.

text.en: I trust your judgment by the lake. Together we'll leave enough fish for the next season.
text.es: Confío en tu criterio junto al lago. Dejaremos suficientes peces para la próxima estación.

text.en: The nets you helped mend are ready, and not a single reed was trampled.
text.es: Las redes que ayudaste a remendar están listas, y no pisamos ni un solo junco.

text.en: You know each animal's pace now. The timid ones come closer when you arrive.
text.es: Ya conoces el ritmo de cada animal. Los tímidos se acercan cuando llegas.

text.en: Your help made the barn calmer today. Even the smallest chick settled down.
text.es: Tu ayuda tranquilizó el establo hoy. Hasta el pollito más pequeño se serenó.

text.en: You've helped preserve the archive with care. I can show you the valley's oldest public map.
text.es: Has cuidado el archivo con esmero. Puedo mostrarte el mapa público más antiguo del valle.

text.en: Those pages you mended will outlast this winter. Thank you for working so gently.
text.es: Las páginas que reparaste resistirán este invierno. Gracias por trabajar con tanto cuidado.
